notes: Source cells use superscript pitch digits; sourceReading flattens only typography. A single 5 remains level pitch 5, not tone category 5.
Cyrillic ә U+04D9 is preserved in source transcription. A future importer must document normalization to IPA ə rather than silently altering the record.
The source labels slash alternatives colloquial then literary in footnote 1, p264. No register is inferred for unslashed cells.
The table uses contextual 特为 and 肋条; this extracts character readings, not whole-word pronunciations.
Gan classification is supported by Xu2022 pp262,264–268. Huai–Yue branch alignment and exact township coordinates still need separate source verification.
Meicheng p269 describes very short transitional i; this preserves the broader table transcription.
No reconstructed, segment-only, Wu, Hui or Mandarin comparison rows are included.

culture.title: Qianshan Museum
culture.text: The museum on Wanguangyuan Road in Meicheng displays Xuejiagang archaeological finds, including jade, stone and pottery objects. Its collections describe the wider Qianshan region.

culture.title: Taiping Pagoda
culture.text: The Northern Song Taiping Pagoda stands within the museum grounds. The old tower and surrounding gardens form a distinct historic site within Meicheng.

soundNotes.title: A medial vowel in the comparison
soundNotes.text: In Table 2, Meicheng’s readings of 狗 and 藕 contain an i medial, while 头, 楼 and 猴 do not. The comparison is limited to these attested characters.

soundNotes.title: Two final patterns
soundNotes.text: Table 3 contrasts the in final of 恩 and 耕 with the central-vowel final of 凳 and 藤. The source treats this as a conditioned historical development, not a spelling rule for all characters.

culture.title: Bamboo weaving on East Street
culture.text: A 2020 local report visits bamboo artisan Zheng Xiuxiang’s shop on East Street in Jiugu village. It documents basket-making as an individual craft practice, not the survey speaker’s occupation.

culture.title: New Year calligraphy
culture.text: In January 2025, county calligraphers visited the Chenwu village square in Jiugu and wrote Spring Festival couplets for local households. The dated event shows how handwritten New Year greetings are shared.
culture.sourceTitle: Anqing Daily · Jiugu Spring Festival couplets, 2025

soundNotes.title: Palatal consonants
soundNotes.text: Jiugu’s Table 2 readings begin with a palatal affricate in 狗 and a palatal nasal in 藕 and 欧. Nearby Meicheng keeps different consonants in the same comparison.

soundNotes.title: Tone distinguishes matching segments
soundNotes.text: The Jiugu readings of 藕 and 欧 have the same segmental transcription but different supplied pitch contours: 442 and 22. These are pitch values, not category numbers.

culture.title: Xiangming Mountain’s temples
culture.text: A county heritage inspection in Yatan documented Mingshan Chan Temple and the nearby Xiayingzhai site on Xiangming Mountain. These are local cultural sites, not linguistic sampling locations.

culture.title: Baoyin Temple Pagoda
culture.text: The same county inspection names Baoyin Temple Pagoda among Yatan’s protected historical attractions. The pagoda offers a separate architectural subject from the mountain temple.

soundNotes.title: Medials are character-specific
soundNotes.text: Yatan’s Table 2 places an i medial in 狗, 藕, 欧, 头 and 楼, while 猴 lacks it. The pattern does not authorize adding a medial to unrecorded words.

soundNotes.title: A different final in 特 and 肋
soundNotes.text: Table 5 records an i medial in Yatan’s 北 and 墨, but not in the contextual readings of 特 in 特为 and 肋 in 肋条. Only the indicated character is transcribed.

culture.title: Liu Wang Liming’s former home
culture.text: The former home in Mingshan village, Xincang, preserves a brick-and-timber courtyard building restored in 2012. The town’s cultural record identifies its location and Huizhou-style architecture.
culture.sourceTitle: Taihu county cultural record · Liu Wang Liming former home and exhibition

culture.title: Women’s education and public life
culture.text: A separate exhibition hall in Mingshan village uses documents to trace Liu Wang Liming’s work in women’s education and social organizations. This is a local biography display, not an attribution of the phonetic survey to her.
culture.sourceTitle: Taihu county cultural record · Liu Wang Liming former home and exhibition

soundNotes.title: Matching segments, contrasting pitch
soundNotes.text: Xincang’s 狗 and 藕 differ in their initial consonants and pitch; 藕 and 欧 share the same segmental transcription but carry contours 31 and 11.

soundNotes.title: Aspiration and pitch both matter
soundNotes.text: In Table 5, Xincang’s 北 and 白 differ in aspiration and contour. Their contrast is preserved in the IPA and HanLingo spelling, rather than collapsed by the shared rhyme.

culture.title: Zhou family buildings
culture.text: Dongzhi’s official heritage register locates Zhou Fu’s reception hall and the Zhou ancestral hall in Zhou village, Meicheng administrative village, Yaodu. These Qing-period buildings are within the wider town.

culture.title: Hualongdong archaeology
culture.text: The town government documents the excavation team at Hualongdong in Wang village. This archaeological site supplies regional historical context; it is not the pronunciation survey site.
culture.sourceTitle: Yaodu town government · Hualongdong excavation visit, 2019

soundNotes.title: Colloquial and literary head readings
soundNotes.text: Table 2 gives two readings of 头 at Yaodu: the colloquial form has an i medial and the literary form does not. Both carry the source contour 224.

soundNotes.title: Same segments, different tone
soundNotes.text: Yaodu’s 藕 and 欧 share their segmental transcription but have contours 35 and 11. The supplied pitch values remain attached to the individual character readings.

culture.title: Gaoqiang costumes and instruments
culture.text: A field visit to Yuexi’s intangible-heritage exhibition in the Wang ancestral hall, Dongshan community, Tiantang, describes embroidered theatre costumes, instruments and documentary displays.
culture.sourceTitle: Student field team report · Yuexi heritage exhibition, 2020

culture.title: Drum storytelling in the community
culture.text: Yuexi’s Women’s Federation reports a 2026 drum-storytelling class in Chengnan community, Tiantang. A local older performer taught the art directly to residents.
culture.sourceTitle: Yuexi Women’s Federation · community drum storytelling, 2026

soundNotes.title: A tonal contrast in one rhyme
soundNotes.text: In Table 3, Tiantang’s 恩 and 硬 share the same segmental transcription but have contours 31 and 22. This is an attested pair, not a reconstructed tone rule.

soundNotes.title: Historical checked characters without a written stop coda
soundNotes.text: Table 4 gives the same ie rhyme and contour 213 for 刻, 格, 隔, 客, 额 and 轭. No final glottal stop is written in these source cells; none is added here.

culture.title: Susong folk singing
culture.text: A local 2024 report documents folk-song teaching and performances in Erlang, including its cultural station’s 2014 gathering. Song performance has its own conventions and is not identical to the citation readings on this page.

culture.title: Harvest celebrations
culture.text: The county’s 2024 harvest-festival report identifies Erlang as its main venue, with agricultural activities and stage performances. This is a documented event rather than an assumed annual custom.

soundNotes.title: A written glottal ending
soundNotes.text: The Erlang cells for 刻, 格, 隔, 客 and 轭 include a glottal-stop coda with level pitch 5. The single digit is a supplied pitch value, not tone category 5.

soundNotes.title: Two registers for 额
soundNotes.text: The source gives colloquial 额 without a written glottal stop and literary 额 with one; both have contour 24. Xu reproduces this Erlang material from Sun Yizhi 2002.

culture.title: Opera troupes and their history
culture.text: Shipai’s Huiban Museum presents the history of Anhui opera troupes, with costumes and materials used in theatre education. A municipal visit documents the museum in the town.
culture.sourceTitle: Anqing municipal report · Shipai opera town, 2026

culture.title: Handmade opera headdresses
culture.text: An official 2026 report describes an elderly artisan teaching cutting, shaping, embroidery and assembly in an opera-headdress workshop on Shipai’s old street.

soundNotes.title: Aspiration and tone
soundNotes.text: Shipai’s Table 5 contrasts unaspirated 北 with aspirated 白. The source also gives different contours, 24 and 13, so both dimensions are retained.

soundNotes.title: Contextual characters
soundNotes.text: The source identifies 特 in 特为 and 肋 in 肋条. Their transcriptions describe those individual characters in context, not the pronunciation of the complete compounds.

culture.title: Dragon boats on Xingfu River
culture.text: A June 2026 reporter’s visit follows the Hongqi village dragon-boat team training on Xingfu River in Saikou. The report records a particular team and season.

culture.title: Poetry at Hongqi Primary School
culture.text: The school’s account of its June 2023 classical-poetry recital describes pupils rehearsing and performing poems. It documents a local educational activity, not the language used in every classroom.
culture.sourceTitle: Hongqi Primary School contributor · poetry recital, 2023

soundNotes.title: A shared rhyme, distinct initials
soundNotes.text: Table 5 gives Saikou’s 北, 墨, 拍 and 麦 the same iæ rhyme and contour 35, while preserving their different initial consonants.

soundNotes.title: A local contrast with Yatan
soundNotes.text: For 特 in 特为, Saikou has an unaspirated initial and an i medial; the source’s Yatan cell has an aspirated initial without that medial. Both source cells carry contour 13.

taihu-yanghe.holdReason: Source names 太湖羊河; contemporary records identify Yanghe village under Niuzhen, but no separately verified village coordinate or historical survey-site reconciliation was obtained. Do not use the Niuzhen town centre.

taihu-jinxi.holdReason: Wikidata Q31852669 supplies two equal-precision coordinates more than 2 km apart. Old/new urban reference remains unresolved; do not choose an anchor silently.

geographyEvidence.method: Exact Chinese town label and direct P131 county match; P625 town anchors, not survey addresses. Meicheng/Tiantang alternatives are less than 1 km apart; choose highest coordinate precision.

classificationEvidence.source: Jing Liwen2025 Language Atlas second-edition county distribution table
classificationEvidence.note: Xu2022 establishes Gan membership for the chosen named settlements; Jing supplies their counties’ Huai–Yue alignment. Dongzhi is mixed Gan/Mandarin/Hui, so only the explicitly Gan Yaodu study is used.

independentReview.scope: 15 visually checked readings only; not full dataset, classification or cultural review
independentReview.rows: All seven Yaodu table2 rows and all eight Meicheng table5 rows
independentReview.result: Exact source-cell, pitch, aspiration, slash register and character-context alignment passed.
